How does keeping unused appliances like blenders plugged into the wall waste electricity?

I would say it does not. An AC appliance current flow is cut off at the switch. A DC item almost always (always?) has an external power transformer (wall wart). In these items the rectifier circuit that converts AC to DC is always powered - primarily we're talking about the primary side of the transformer that steps the voltage down from 120/240 to ~5VAC.

The issue is that there is no power switch on that side. Thus there is always current flow, if memory serves around 7 watts. The thing is that people, be they eco-terrorists, or just reporters out for cheap headlines surmised, probably quite accurately, that given 300 million people this does add up to a lot of wasted amperes. They fail to mention that leaving the bedroom light on one day uses more electricity than all your power cubes for the entire year -- because that doesn't make good headlines.

Regardless there are new regulations with which I am only somewhat familiar. They call for "smart" wall warts that can detect when a Load is not attached and can hugely reduce current flow. Some is always going to be required so the power supply can detect when a load is attached. But the drop was very dramatic, just enough to power the detection itself e.g. from 7W to like 1/4W or something.

Am I really wasting electricity when I keep unused appliances like a blender plugged into the wall, or is that just a myth?

Unless you leave them running, you aren't wasting electricity. If the appliance in question has something like an "always on" digital display (like a clock) it uses a very trivial amount of electricity.

Your Ac and heat are far more wasteful of electricity than any lightbulb, usb charger, or TV could ever be. Turn that shit off or down when you're out. A blender probably isn't wasting electricity since it's not drawing anything unless it's somehow smart... Still haven't heard of the smart blender though, maybe next year?

It depends on the design of the appliance. If it's something that has a 'hard' switch, a switch that cuts the ac power off to the device completely, just turning it off will prevent it from consuming power. Many devices these days have an electronic switch system that consumes a small amount of power and remains on standby, ready to switch the actual device on when you want to turn it on.

A computer in sleep mode still draws power. It draws several watts even when it's shut down, depending on what motherboard you have and how you set your BIOS, it will keep some components powered, like USBs, ethernet port (for wake-on-lan), some leds. But I'm pretty sure you waste more body energy to unplug your computer than your computer is using, you got my point. Blenders, power chargers and so one "waste" so little energy. For all your standby/powered off electronic in your house, maybe you'll pay one dolar less if you unplug them.
